scope: Literature and mechanism synthesis for proposal 07: asymmetric soft-boundary PD, joint L1/L2/L3 KV-cache and prefill-placement scheduling under a fixed GPU budget, and gradual D-to-prefill-heavy adaptation. This record does not establish novelty, framework support, or serving performance. Proposal 07 is a design; no implementation or GPU experiment was run.

new_paper_60.identity_note: Title and venue verified on the official PMLR v306 index and paper page; the archived PDF is the official proceedings version, not the arXiv v2.

mechanism_readings.finding: A session is bound to a decode worker. Incremental prefill can execute locally on that worker or remotely on a prefill worker; remote execution may read history KV from the decode worker and returns only incremental KV. Routing uses windowed TTFT/ITL slack and profiled local/remote cost.
Offline deployment planning has an explicit fixed total-GPU constraint, but is separate from online per-request prefill routing.

DualPath loads hit KV either directly into the prefill engine or into a decode engine followed by transfer to prefill. Prefill remains on P. Splitting one request across both read paths is left as future work in §6.1, lines 859-863.
PPD routes Turn 2+ append-prefill to decode nodes holding local cached KV; the implementation uses a local prefix cache and session table. It does not study external-storage loading paths.
Kairos executes deflected prefill on decode nodes as chunked prefill under TBT constraints, with per-request chunk schedules.

Llumnix provides live request/KV migration to support continuous rescheduling and instance draining.

mechanism_readings.finding: Provides the distributed KV-cache/storage baseline; no new performance claim is made in proposal 07.
Strata covers host-memory/external-storage data management, opportunistic prefetch and I/O-aware scheduling; proposal 07 uses it as a tiered-cache and I/O baseline.

design_boundaries: P and D are asymmetric: P is prefill-priority, D is decode-priority with bounded append-prefill; P is not assumed to become a decode worker.
L1/L2/L3 are proposal-specific logical names for device HBM, host DRAM and external persistent/distributed KV storage respectively; they are not claimed as a universal framework naming standard.
The four L3 paths are A=P-load/P-compute, B=D-load/P-compute, C=D-load/D-compute, D=P-load/D-compute. Decode stays on the selected D; P-local decode is not assumed.

Gradual adaptation primarily targets D-to-prefill-heavy: old decodes continue while controlled new prefill is admitted. Full physical P-role conversion is claimed only if the instance supports all required capabilities.
P-to-D conversion, arbitrary full-prefill on D, active request migration and split-load are conditional extensions, not first-version claims.
research_increment_to_test: Whether the joint cache-source and compute-placement action set outperforms DualPath-style loading-only and PPD/AMPD-style local/remote-prefill policies.
Whether admitting controlled new prefill while old decodes continue improves cumulative SLO delivery relative to FluidPD-style drain-first role switching and Splitwise-style temporary mixed pooling.
Whether each of the four paths has a non-dominated operating region; paths that never win should be removed.
